:::{#exm-min-entropy}
#### Min-entropy of a three-valued random variable

<!-- no-figure: the example is one number -->

Let $X$ take three values with [probabilities](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) $1/2$, $1/4$ and $1/4$.
The code below finds the largest probability and the [min-entropy](#def-min-entropy),
with base-2 [logarithms](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#def-logarithm).

```{r}
#| label: min-entropy
p <- c(1 / 2, 1 / 4, 1 / 4)
max_prob <- max(p)
min_entropy <- -log2(max_prob)
c(max_prob = max_prob, min_entropy = min_entropy)
```

The largest probability is $`r max_prob`$,
so the min-entropy is $\renyientropyf{\infty}{X} = `r min_entropy`$ [bit](entropy.qmd#def-bit).

:::
